modeReason: The story of a man winning a religious exemption from AI reaches relevance 12 (novelty 3 × magnitude 2 × breadth 2), and two other stories reach 8, both above the fresh threshold of 8, so today stands on its own rather than continuing yesterday's thread.
phrase: A humanist won a legal exemption from having to use AI at all. A top judge says AI should decide people's court cases instead.
phraseAlternatives: One man got legal permission to avoid AI completely. A senior judge wants to let AI decide court cases instead.
A religious exemption frees one man from AI entirely. A top judge argues AI should rule on civil lawsuits.
While one man is excused from AI, a senior judge wants it to decide court cases instead.
A man won the right to live without AI. A judge wants AI to decide who wins in court.

brief.concept: A person stands behind a small fence marked EXEMPT holding an exemption paper while a robot reaches toward them from outside it; across the scene, a human judge hands a gavel to a robot taking a seat on the court bench.
brief.metaphor: One person wins the right to be left out of AI, while a court hands AI the power to decide everyone else's cases.
